title: P/T Petri net (model-check engine input)
description: A place/transition net in the sense of Holzmann, Design and Validation of Computer Protocols, §8.10: places carry tokens, a transition is enabled when every input place holds at least the arc weight, firing removes the input weights and adds the output weights. Arc weights > 1 extend Holzmann's one-token arcs. Inhibitor arcs are recognised only to be rejected: Holzmann's §8.10 net has no negation ('the absence of a token cannot be tested'), and the engine encodes exactly that class as byte variables and guarded commands, as in Promela - examples/App_C/petrinet1. The frontend (frontend/petri) validates against this schema by hand-written checks that mirror it clause by clause.

name.description: Model name used in reports. Defaults to the file name.

places.description: Places in declaration order; the order fixes the state-vector layout.

transitions.description: Transitions in declaration order; the order is the deterministic firing order of the explorer.

identifier.description: Names double as IR variable names, so they follow identifier syntax.

initial.description: Initial marking of the place; must not exceed the capacity.

capacity.description: Maximum tokens the place may hold (the Promela `byte` domain of the reference encoding). Exceeding it during exploration is a modelling error: every property is reported invalid-model.

line.description: Optional source line for the mapping table.

weight.description: Tokens moved along the arc when the transition fires.

inhibitor.description: Input arcs only. An inhibitor arc enables the transition when the place is EMPTY. It is part of the schema so that the frontend can name the offending arc when rejecting it; the engine never translates inhibitor arcs (Holzmann §8.10: the P/T net cannot express negation, and the reference Promela encoding tests only x > 0).

inputs.description: Input arcs (place → transition). A transition without inputs is always enabled.

outputs.description: Output arcs (transition → place). `inhibitor` is not allowed here.
